title: Constant towers and evaluations preserve the unbounded derived adjunctions of a ringed morphism
statement:
Let $u:(\mathcal U,\mathcal O_{\mathcal U})\to(\mathcal V,\mathcal O_{\mathcal V})$ be a morphism of small ringed sites [def-weil-size-convention] whose coefficient map $u^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathcal V}\to\mathcal O_{\mathcal U}$ is an isomorphism, so that module inverse image $u^*$ is exact. Use unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the canonical derived adjunction $u^*\dashv Ru_*$, with $Ru_*$ computed on K-injective complexes [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Put $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$ and, for $W=\mathcal U,\mathcal V$, let $\mathcal T_W=\operatorname{Fun}(J,\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_W))$ be the strict tower category [def-weil-inverse-system], realized as modules on the small diagram site [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], with termwise inverse image $u^*_{\mathcal T}$, termwise direct image $u^{\mathcal T}_*$ and the canonical derived adjunction $u^*_{\mathcal T}\dashv\mathscr R_u$. Let $\Delta_W:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_W)\to\mathcal T_W$ be the constant-tower functor and $\operatorname{ev}_n:\mathcal T_W\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_W)$ evaluation at $n\geq1$. Then:
(1) $\operatorname{ev}_1\dashv\Delta_W$, and the functors $\Delta_W$ and $\operatorname{ev}_n$ are exact and carry K-injective complexes to K-injective complexes.
(2) The termwise equalities $\Delta_{\mathcal U}u^*=u^*_{\mathcal T}\Delta_{\mathcal V}$ and $\operatorname{ev}_nu^*_{\mathcal T}=u^*\operatorname{ev}_n$ descend to the derived categories, and there are natural isomorphisms
$$b^\Delta:\Delta_{\mathcal V}Ru_*\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathscr R_u\Delta_{\mathcal U},\qquad b^n:\operatorname{ev}_n\mathscr R_u\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_*\operatorname{ev}_n,$$
represented on a K-injective complex $I$ of $\mathcal O_{\mathcal U}$-modules by the identity of $\Delta_{\mathcal V}u_*I$, respectively on a K-injective complex $I$ of towers by the identity of $u_*I_n$.
(3) These comparisons carry derived adjuncts to derived adjuncts: for every derived morphism $t:u^*M\to N$ the derived adjunct of $\Delta_{\mathcal U}(t)$ is $b^\Delta_N\circ\Delta_{\mathcal V}(t^\sharp)$, and for every derived morphism $t:u^*_{\mathcal T}M\to N$ of towers the derived adjunct of $\operatorname{ev}_n(t)$ is $b^n_N\circ\operatorname{ev}_n(t^\sharp)$. In particular they identify the derived units and counits.
(4) Consequently, for a commutative square of such morphisms of small ringed sites whose inverse-image composition comparisons are computed termwise, $\Delta$ carries the ordinary derived square mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] at $K$ to the termwise derived square mate at $\Delta K$, and $\operatorname{ev}_n$ carries the termwise derived square mate at a tower $K_\bullet$ to the ordinary one at $K_n$, after the isomorphisms of (2).
These are equalities of actual derived morphisms. No faithfulness of derived evaluation and no invertibility of either mate is asserted.

proof.text: For a tower $T$ write $T_{n,1}:T_n\to T_1$ for the composite transition. The maps $\operatorname{Hom}(T,\Delta A)\to\operatorname{Hom}(T_1,A)$ and $a\mapsto(a\circ T_{n,1})_{n\geq1}$ are inverse: naturality along $n\to1$ forces every component, and the transition composition law verifies naturality of the displayed family. They are natural in $T,A$, proving $\operatorname{ev}_1\dashv\Delta$. The levelwise kernel and cokernel formulas of the cited node make $\operatorname{ev}_n$ exact and make $\Delta$ exact, since the kernel or cokernel of a constant morphism is the corresponding constant tower.

source.place: Tag 08BJ, exact-left-adjoint criterion; the terminal-index adjunction is the explicit elementary argument here

proof.text: Apply the exact-left-adjoint criterion to $\operatorname{ev}_1\dashv\Delta$: $\Delta$ preserves K-injectives. Evaluation preserves K-injectives by the cited evaluation theorem, reindexing $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$ by $n\mapsto n-1$ if necessary. The exact coefficient-preserving $u^*$ and its termwise tower functor are left adjoint to $u_*$ and $u_*^{\mathcal T}$ respectively, so these two right adjoints also preserve K-injectives. The tower adjunction has the ordinary unit and counit at every index: their naturality makes them tower maps and their two triangle identities hold at each component.

source.place: Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives; evaluation theorem specialized to the inverse-sequence poset

proof.text: The small diagram-site realization identifies each tower category with modules on a small ringed site. Thus the cited resolution theorem applies both to the two original module categories and to their tower categories: they are Grothendieck abelian and have unbounded K-injective resolutions. Exact-functor descent applies to $u^*,u^*_{\mathcal T},\Delta,\operatorname{ev}_n$. The two termwise inverse-image identities therefore descend with their specified localization comparisons; uniqueness on natural transformations follows from localization's universal property. Total right derived direct images are computed on K-injectives. Its hypothesis on the homotopy-category functor is satisfied: an additive functor on complexes commutes with the shift and the cone matrix (which uses only finite biproducts), so its composite with localization is triangulated.

proof.text: For $N\cong QI$ with $I$ K-injective on $\mathcal U$, step 2 makes $\Delta_{\mathcal U}I$ K-injective. The two sides of $b^\Delta_N$ are therefore represented by the same complex $\Delta_{\mathcal V}u_*I=u_*^{\mathcal T}\Delta_{\mathcal U}I$; take its identity, using the total-derived comparisons. This defines a natural isomorphism on all derived objects: a derived map $QI\to QI'$ between K-injectives is the image of a unique homotopy class $[a]:I\to I'$ by the cited Hom bijection. Both sides carry it to the homotopy class of the same tower map $\Delta_{\mathcal V}u_*a=u_*^{\mathcal T}\Delta_{\mathcal U}a$. Changes of K-injective representative are represented by homotopy equivalences by the same node, and the displayed equality intertwines those equivalences too. Hence the identities are independent of representatives, natural, and invertible.

source.place: Tags 070I and 070K, lemma-K-injective and lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies; constant-tower identity application

proof.text: For a K-injective tower complex $I$, step 2 makes $I_n$ K-injective. Thus $\operatorname{ev}_n\mathscr R_u(QI)$ and $Ru_*\operatorname{ev}_n(QI)$ are both represented by $u_*I_n$; let $b^n_{QI}$ be its identity under the total-derived comparisons. A derived map between K-injective tower complexes is represented by a unique homotopy class of tower maps. Evaluation and direct image in either order give exactly the same evaluated map. The Hom bijection and the homotopy-equivalence assertion for K-injectives consequently make these identities independent of representatives and natural, exactly as in step 4. This proves the comparison assertions of (2) with the required normalizations.

source.place: Tags 070I and 070K, lemma-K-injective and lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies; evaluation identity application

proof.text:
Use $F=u^*$, $G=u_*$, or their tower versions. For a complex $M$ and K-injective $I$, the Hom bijection into K-injectives, the homotopy adjunction, and step 2 give the natural composite
$$\operatorname{Hom}_D(FQM,QI)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_K(FM,I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_K(M,GI)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_D(QM,QGI).$$
For a chain map $a:FM\to I$ it sends $Q(a)$ to $Q(G(a)\circ\eta_M^0)$. This is the canonical derived adjunction, with the canonical total-derived comparison on $GI$: apply the cited normalization theorem with left resolving class all of $K(\mathcal A)$, which is allowed because $F$ is exact and hence inverts quasi-isomorphisms after localization. Its formula identifies this composite with the specified canonical adjunction, rather than merely producing an unspecified adjunction.

source.place: Tags 070I and 0DVC/0FND; canonical normalization also sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint

proof.text:
Represent $M$ by a complex and $N$ by a K-injective $I$. Every derived $t:u^*M\to N$ is represented by a chain map $a:u^*M\to I$ modulo homotopy. Since $\Delta I$ is K-injective, the corresponding tower map represents $\Delta(t)$. The two ordinary transposes satisfy the equality of actual chain maps
$$u_*^{\mathcal T}(\Delta a)\circ\eta^{0,\mathcal T}_{\Delta M}=\Delta(u_*a\circ\eta^0_M),$$
because both the unit and the functors are termwise. Applying the normalized Hom formula of step 6 and the identity normalization of $b^\Delta$ in step 4 proves
$$(\Delta t)^\sharp=b^\Delta_N\circ\Delta(t^\sharp).$$
The Hom bijection justifies the representative for every derived $t$, including unbounded $M$; replacement is allowed by the independence proved in step 4.

source.place: Tags 070I and 0DVC, resolved transpose formula applied to constant towers

proof.text:
Represent the source tower by a complex $M$ and the target by a K-injective tower complex $I$. A derived $t:u^*_{\mathcal T}M\to N$ is represented by a chain map $a:u^*_{\mathcal T}M\to I$, since its target is K-injective. Evaluating gives a chain representative of $\operatorname{ev}_n(t)$ into K-injective $I_n$. Its transpose is
$$u_*(a_n)\circ\eta^0_{M_n}=\bigl(u_*^{\mathcal T}(a)\circ\eta^{0,\mathcal T}_M\bigr)_n.$$
The normalized Hom formula of step 6 and the identity normalization of step 5 therefore give
$$(\operatorname{ev}_n t)^\sharp=b^n_N\circ\operatorname{ev}_n(t^\sharp).$$
This argument computes in the Hom sets of the derived categories themselves; it does not infer equality of tower morphisms from equality of evaluations.

source.place: Tags 070I and 0DVC, resolved transpose formula applied to evaluation

proof.text:
The unit is the transpose of $1_{u^*M}$ and the counit is the inverse transpose of $1_{Ru_*N}$. Substitution in steps 7 and 8 gives
$$\eta^{\mathcal T}_{\Delta M}=b^\Delta_{u^*M}\circ\Delta\eta_M,\qquad \Delta\varepsilon_N=\varepsilon^{\mathcal T}_{\Delta N}\circ u^*_{\mathcal T}(b^\Delta_N),$$
$$\eta_{M_n}=b^n_{u^*_{\mathcal T}M}\circ\operatorname{ev}_n\eta^{\mathcal T}_M,\qquad \operatorname{ev}_n\varepsilon^{\mathcal T}_N=\varepsilon_{N_n}\circ u^*(b^n_N).$$
For example the inverse transpose of $b^\Delta_N$ is $\varepsilon^{\mathcal T}_{\Delta N}\circ u^*_{\mathcal T}(b^\Delta_N)$, which proves the first counit identity; the second is the same substitution into step 8. All inverse-image identifications here are those of step 3.

source.place: Adjunction definitions: unit/counit as transposes of identities; substitution in steps 7 and 8

proof.text:
Write the square as $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $h:X'\to X$, with inverse-image comparison $\theta:f'^*g^*\xrightarrow{\sim}h^*f^*$. In this step $X,Y,X',Y'$ denote ringed sites. By the definition of a square mate, its component $E_K:g^*Rf_*K\to Rf'_*h^*K$ is the adjunct under $f'^*\dashv Rf'_*$ of
$$c_K=h^*(\varepsilon^f_K)\circ\theta_{Rf_*K}.$$
The tower mate $E^{\mathcal T}$ is defined by the identical formula with tower functors. The hypothesis on the square identifies $\Delta\theta$ and $\operatorname{ev}_n\theta^{\mathcal T}$ with the corresponding tower and ordinary comparisons. We now compare adjuncts using these formulas, which is a direct check of the specified mates.

For constants the desired precise equality is
$$E^{\mathcal T}_{\Delta K}\circ g_{\mathcal T}^*(b^\Delta_{f,K})=b^\Delta_{f',h^*K}\circ\Delta(E_K).$$
By step 7 the transpose of the right side is $\Delta(c_K)$. The transpose of the left side, by the mate definition, is
$$h_{\mathcal T}^*\varepsilon^{f,\mathcal T}_{\Delta K}\circ\theta^{\mathcal T}_{\mathscr R_f\Delta K}\circ f'^*_{\mathcal T}g^*_{\mathcal T}(b^\Delta_{f,K}).$$
Naturality of $\theta^{\mathcal T}$ rewrites this as
$$h_{\mathcal T}^*\bigl(\varepsilon^{f,\mathcal T}_{\Delta K}\circ f^*_{\mathcal T}(b^\Delta_{f,K})\bigr)\circ\theta^{\mathcal T}_{\Delta Rf_*K}=\Delta(c_K),$$
where the equality uses the constant counit equation of step 9 and the termwise comparison of step 10. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection gives the asserted equality of derived tower morphisms.

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change; naturality and the constant counit equation

proof.text:
For evaluation the precise equality is
$$b^n_{f',h^*_{\mathcal T}K}\circ\operatorname{ev}_n(E^{\mathcal T}_K)=E_{K_n}\circ g^*(b^n_{f,K}).$$
By step 8 the left side has transpose $\operatorname{ev}_n(c^{\mathcal T}_K)$. The right side has transpose
$$h^*\varepsilon^f_{K_n}\circ\theta_{Rf_*K_n}\circ f'^*g^*(b^n_{f,K}).$$
Naturality of $\theta$ rewrites it as
$$h^*\bigl(\varepsilon^f_{K_n}\circ f^*(b^n_{f,K})\bigr)\circ\theta_{\operatorname{ev}_n\mathscr R_fK}=\operatorname{ev}_n(c^{\mathcal T}_K),$$
by the evaluated counit equation of step 9 and the termwise comparison of step 10. The ordinary derived adjunction Hom bijection gives the equality. Steps 11 and 12 establish (4) without assuming that evaluation is faithful or that either square mate is invertible.

source.place: Tag 07A7, remark-base-change; naturality and the evaluation counit equation
